sentences.text: The only known fossil of Torotix is a partial upper arm bone found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
Later researchers suggested that Torotix was more likely related to the Charadriiformes, which includes waders and shorebirds.
More recent comparative studies have found Torotix to be most similar to the order Pelecaniformes.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Torotix as Pelecaniformes.
Torotix lived at the very end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 66 million years ago.
This animal existed during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It inhabited the shores of the Western Interior Seaway, though it remains unclear if it was a seabird or a freshwater bird.
